title: Шоколадный фондан и задержка времени  (Chocolate Fondant and Buying Time)

segments.t: Outside, Nastya rejects the SUV because of the pollution it releases into the atmosphere. Inside the kitchen, word arrives that the sheikh has finished his business talks early, forcing Barinov to improvise a way to entertain him.
Ты знаешь вообще, какой от него выброс в атмосферу?
Спасибо, не надо.
Шейх закончил переговоры.
Где обещанный десерт?
Луи, иди сюда скорее!
Сделай ещё один шоколадный фондан.
А я найду, чем занять гостя.
Шеф, но десерт уже готов!
Мне нужно выиграть ещё двадцать минут.
И что вы собираетесь делать в зале?
Сейчас увидишь настоящее шоу.
Удачи вам, шеф!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Ты знаешь вообще, какой от него выброс в атмосферу?

'Do you even know what kind of emissions it puts into the atmosphere?' Asking whether Barinov even know what kind of emissions it puts into the atmosphere is how Nastya puts Barinov on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Спасибо, не надо.
'Thank you, no need.' With the plan and shift in play, Nastya keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Шейх закончил переговоры.
'The sheikh has finished his negotiations.' Once the sheikh has finished his negotiations, Louis can finally tell Barinov what he means.
Где обещанный десерт?

'Where is the promised dessert?' Asking where the promised dessert is is how Louis puts Barinov on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Луи, иди сюда скорее!
'Louis, come here quickly!' Coming here quickly shows Barinov is done holding back.
Сделай ещё один шоколадный фондан.
'Make one more chocolate fondant.' Noting that Louis should make one more chocolate fondant keeps Barinov's side of the story simple and clear.
А я найду, чем занять гостя.
'And I will find something to keep the guest occupied.' Mentioning that he will find something to keep the guest occupied moves the talk in a new direction.
Шеф, но десерт уже готов!
'Chef, but the dessert is already ready!' Saying that the dessert is already ready is how Louis takes charge of the moment.
Мне нужно выиграть ещё двадцать минут.

'I need to buy twenty more minutes.' Explaining that he needs to buy twenty more minutes lays the cards on the table for Louis. There is no "you" needed in the Russian here: one short word states the rule for everyone in the room.
И что вы собираетесь делать в зале?

'And what are you going to do in the dining room?' Wondering what Barinov going to do in the dining room is is how Louis puts Barinov on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Сейчас увидишь настоящее шоу.
'Right now you will see a real show.' Barinov reminds Louis that right now Louis will see a real show before the moment passes.
Удачи вам, шеф!

'Good luck to you, Chef!' With the conversation and work at stake, Louis reacts without holding back. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Ты знаешь вообще, какой от него выброс в атмосферу?
Спасибо, не надо.
Шейх закончил переговоры.
Где обещанный десерт?
Луи, иди сюда скорее!
Сделай ещё один шоколадный фондан.
А я найду, чем занять гостя.
Шеф, но десерт уже готов!
Мне нужно выиграть ещё двадцать минут.
И что вы собираетесь делать в зале?
Сейчас увидишь настоящее шоу.
Удачи вам, шеф!
Grabbing a rolling cart of kitchen tools and ingredients, Barinov wheels it out to the sheikh's table to put on a culinary magic show. Until next time!
До встречи!
